subject: Atlas AI - Dedicated pool turn-up and surge guardrails
messages:
From: Anya Petrov <anya@atlasai.com>

Subject: Atlas AI - Dedicated pool turn-up and surge guardrails

Hi Vivek / Monica,

Thanks for taking this on. We’re excited to move our dedicated GPU pool with Redwood into pilot next month. Quick context: Atlas AI will be serving a mix of synchronous inference (low-latency chat) and batch embeddings jobs for analytics. Expected steady-state: 1200 qps peak daytime across our US customers; observed short spikes roughly 2x for 10-20 minute windows during product releases.

Two asks to kick off implementation planning:
- A recommended primary region(s) and a fallback region for burst capacity (we prefer US multi-region redundancy).
- A proposed baseline pool size and burst/autoscale guardrails that balance latency SLA (95th <= 220ms) with cost.

I attached a small traffic snapshot (atlas-region-map.csv) and can share longer logs if helpful. Can we get a high-level plan and a rough schedule for 1) provisioning, 2) smoke testing, and 3) go-live cutover? We’d like a canary in staging before the production switch—targeting pilot go-live week of Sep 14.

Thanks,
Anya
Head of Platform Engineering
Atlas AI
(ops@atlasai.com)

Subject: Re: Atlas AI - Dedicated pool turn-up and surge guardrails

Anya — thanks for the clear context and the sample. High level response below; I'll follow up with a short runbook and a draft burst policy (attached).

Summary recommendation (preview):
- Primary region: us-east1 (closest to your largest customer base and lower tail latency historically)
- Cold-fallback region: us-west1 (warm standby; cross-region KV cache pre-warm)
- Baseline pool: 8 x A100 equivalent for steady-state (handles ~1k sustained qps given your mix; we’ll confirm sizing after load test)
- Burst window: allow up to +30% burst on top of baseline using Dedicated burst credits; auto-failover to shared-hosted capacity (with slightly higher latency) if both regions saturated.

Next steps I'll take this week:
1) Share "turnup-runbook-v1.pdf" with orchestration checklist (provisioning, IP allowlists, KMS config).
2) Draft autoscale and burst policy ("burst-policy-draft.md") with stepwise scale increments, warm pool warming triggers, and cooldown timers.
3) Schedule a 45-min architect sync (Propose: Thu Aug 24 10am ET) to align on prewarm TTLs and the canary plan.

Can you confirm the Sep 14 pilot target and whether you need HIPAA-level logging for that pilot? Also, any procurement/PO timing we should be aware of?

Vivek
Sr. Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: Atlas AI pool turn-up - quick alignment

Monica / Rishi / Marissa —

Looping you in to coordinate provisioning and ops handoff. Key points from Anya: 1. steady ~1.2k qps daytime, 2. 10-20m 2x spikes, target pilot week Sep 14.

Proposed internal checklist (short):
- Procurement: confirm commitment window and billing start date (Marissa)
- Infra provisioning: reserve 8 A100 equiv in us-east1 + warm 4 in us-west1; plan for burst pool access to host-shared GPUs if needed (Rishi)
- Networking: get Atlas allowlist and private peering tickets; provide NAT/egress notes (Monica)
- SRE test plan: 2-step canary (staging smoke + progressive traffic ramp over 72h) and a rollback plan tied to error-rate thresholds (we own cutover)

Questions for team:
- Rishi: do we want preemptible-backed burst vs. queued shared-hosted burst? Costs differ; preemptible can save cost but increases churn.
- Monica: can you confirm default KV-cache warm TTLs we should configure before canary?

I'll take owner for the customer-facing runbook and the draft burst policy. Please add items to ATLAS-3472 and I’ll assign owners.

-V
From: Anya Petrov <anya@atlasai.com>

Subject: Re: Atlas AI - Dedicated pool turn-up and surge guardrails

Thanks Vivek — this reads well. A couple clarifications from our side before the Thu sync:

- Regional failover: we prefer user-facing traffic to stay within US regions. If us-east1 is saturated, we want failover to us-west1 first, then to hosted shared fallback. Can you confirm cross-region failover latency delta?

- Autoscale targets: our engineering lead asked if we can limit scale steps to +2 GPUs per minute with a maximum burst of +3 GPUs above baseline at once, rather than large jumps. That helps with model warm-up costs.

- Preemptible vs shared-hosted: we’d prefer preemptible for short spikes if it preserves the 95th latency target — cost wins are important for our SRE budget.

We can provide a PO by Sep 3 if that helps with reservation timing. Confirming HIPAA: not required for pilot.

-Anya
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Petrov <anya@atlasai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-25T16:47:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Atlas AI - Dedicated pool turn-up and surge guardrails

Anya — thanks, answers and firmed plan below. I’ll present this at the Thu sync and update the runbook.

Regional failover and expected delta:
- Primary: us-east1 (expected 95th tail + baseline ~180–210ms)
- Warm-fallback: us-west1 (cross-region tail adds ~25–40ms depending on routing and KV cache locality).
- Hosted shared fallback: additional +80–120ms. We will configure the routing policy to prefer us-west1 before falling back to shared.

Autoscale/burst policy (draft final):
- Baseline pool: 8 x A100 equiv in us-east1 (reserved).
- Warm standby: 4 x A100 equiv in us-west1 (kept warm, minimal cost overhead via reduced clock frequency).
- Scale step: +2 GPUs per minute; maximum concurrent burst +3 GPUs above baseline via reserved burst credits.
- Burst overflow: if reserved credits exhausted, use preemptible fleet first (preferred by Atlas), then fall back to hosted shared capacity as a last resort.
- Warm-up: KV cache pre-warm trigger at 60% of baseline utilization; model pre-warm window 90s per instance.
- Cooldown: 5-minute cooldown after a downscale to avoid flapping.
- SLO gating: automatic rollback to staged baseline if 95th latency > 300ms for >5m during canary.

Operational notes / timeline:
- Provisioning hold: if Atlas submits PO by Sep 3 we can lock the baseline reservation for Sep 7 provisioning.
- Staging canary: Sep 10 — runbook smoke tests + perf injection.
- Pilot go-live: target Sep 14 with progressive ramp to full traffic over 72h (ATLAS-3472 will track this).

Action items:
- Atlas: PO by Sep 3 (Anya)
- Redwood: Create provisioning ticket and reserve instances (Rishi)
- Redwood: Finalize runbook and attach test checklist to ATLAS-3472 (Vivek)
- Redwood: Networking allowlist template to Atlas (Monica)

If this looks good I’ll convert the burst-policy-draft.md into a signed MOP and link it to the Jira ticket.

Best,
